answer: In a PoA attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks, causing influence to decay across transitions rather than multiply within a coalition. Adversarial Sybil clusters usually expose sparse external cuts with low conductance; conductance and min-cut transitivity bounds therefore limit the probability that honest-rooted walks enter them, bounding their aggregate stationary mass and voting weight unless they obtain many independent attestations. Ferrous identities, tide signals, and saffron metadata cannot evade this structural constraint.
